extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners (attorneys and agents) and counsel who appear before the USPTO/PTAB; OED/ethics counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedures governing professional responsibility and discipline for practitioners who practice before the USPTO, with an emphasis on prohibited ex parte communications with PTAB judges and related sanctions and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdiction of USPTO Director over practitioner discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over disciplinary matters pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 2(b)(2)(D) and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.19 and 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This establishes the Office's authority to approve settlement agreements and impose discipline on registered patent practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicable professional conduct rules (timing-sensitive)
rubrics_metrics.description: Because the events occurred prior to May 3, 2013, the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility (37 C.F.R. § 10.20 et seq.) is applicable; effective May 3, 2013 the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.101–11.901) apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify which version of the rules applies based on the date of the conduct; citations to the correct regulatory scheme are required when evaluating alleged misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on written communications with a judge without copying opposing counsel (37 C.F.R. § 10.93(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: It is a violation to communicate in writing with a judge before whom a proceeding is pending in an adversary proceeding on the merits of the case without providing a copy of the writing to opposing counsel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order specifically finds that Respondent violated 37 C.F.R. § 10.93(b) by authorizing/approving an email to a PTAB judge that was not copied to opposing counsel. When evaluating practitioner's conduct, check whether written communications to adjudicators were shared with opposing counsel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on ex parte contact with the PTAB (37 C.F.R. § 42.5(d) and Practice Guide)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ex parte contact with the Board is prohibited except under extremely limited circumstances as specifically set forth in the Board's rules; the January 15 email was held to be an improper ex parte communication and an improper attempt to file a reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult 37 C.F.R. § 42.5(d) and the Office Patent Trial Practice Guide (77 Fed. Reg. 48756, 48758) for limits; an email sent to the Board about substantive matter without serving opposing counsel constitutes improper ex parte contact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to provide opposing counsel a copy of communications to the judge/Board
rubrics_metrics.description: When communicating in writing with a judge before whom a proceeding is pending in an adversary proceeding, practitioners must provide a copy to opposing counsel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to provide a copy is a regulatory violation (see 37 C.F.R. § 10.93(b)) and may be treated as ex parte contact; best practice is to serve opposing counsel on any substantive communications to the Board or judge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted procedure for requesting a conference call with the PTAB (practical guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical guidance (as memorialized by PTAB staff in an email) was that a practitioner should send an email to trials@uspto.gov explaining the need for a conference call; copying opposing counsel is optional, and the judge will decide whether a call is necessary and propose times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order notes there was 'no documentation for this type of procedure' and the staff were 'figuring it out as they go'—so practitioners should follow formal rules if unclear and, when in doubt, include opposing counsel to avoid ex parte issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supervisory responsibility for communications by subordinate counsel
rubrics_metrics.description: A supervising practitioner is responsible for authorizing and approving communications sent by subordinate or associate counsel; Respondent authorized and had full knowledge of the January 15 email and its contents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supervising attorneys may be disciplined for improper communications sent by attorneys they supervise; ensure supervision and review procedures prevent improper ex parte contact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions available: public reprimand and publication (37 C.F.R. § 11.59 compliance)
rubrics_metrics.description: The agreed-upon sanction in this matter was a public reprimand; the OED Director shall comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 and publish the Final Order in the OED electronic FOIA Reading Room and publish a Notice of Reprimand in the Official Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary outcomes may include public reprimand and publication of the decision; practitioners should be aware that discipline can be publicly posted and published by the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement agreements can resolve disciplinary action but do not preclude future consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: This action is the result of a settlement agreement between Respondent and the OED Director pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 2(b)(2)(D) and relevant regulations; however, nothing in the Agreement or Final Order prevents the Office from considering the record in future complaints or proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlements may resolve a present matter but the underlying record can be used subsequently as aggravating evidence or to rebut representations in later disciplinary matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of prior disciplinary record as aggravating factor or rebuttal evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may consider the record of this disciplinary proceeding (including this Final Order) when addressing any further complaint of the same or similar misconduct or in any future disciplinary proceeding against the respondent as (i) an aggravating factor in determining discipline and/or (ii) to rebut statements by or on respondent's behalf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior discipline can increase future sanctions or be used to challenge credibility or representations; practitioners should understand long-term consequences of disciplinary findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs in settlement
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent shall each bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of this Agreement and any Final Order approving this Agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement terms may specify cost allocation; this Order reflects a common compromise where each side bears its own costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference to substantive correction of filings (example of allowed post-order action)
rubrics_metrics.description: After the Order, Patent Owner was permitted to file a five-page reply acknowledging and correcting a mathematical error in its preliminary response; Patent Owner deleted the statement and arguments based on the mathematical error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an error in a filing is identified, the Board may allow a limited reply or correction; however, practitioners should not attempt to correct or draw the Board's attention ex parte without serving opposing counsel.
